```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("../code"))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from osim import natl_sim as ns

REPS = list(range(10))
PAR_LAB = {"phi": "Variance", "th_lon": "Zonal range", "th_lat": "Meridional range", "th_t": "Temporal range"}
LAYER_LAB = {"ohc_15_700": "15-700 m", "ohc_700_2000": "700-2000 m"}

def _emit(s=""):
    print(s)
    sys.stdout.flush()

def _show_fig(fig):
    display(fig)
    plt.close(fig)

def _tabs(items):
    _emit("::: {.panel-tabset}")
    for name, show in items:
        _emit(f"\n## {name}\n")
        show()
    _emit(":::")

def _layer_par_tabs(fig):
    _tabs([(LAYER_LAB[l], lambda l=l: _tabs([(PAR_LAB[p], lambda p=p: _show_fig(fig(l, p))) for p in ns.COV_PARAMS]))
           for l in ns.LAYER_NAMES])
```

Each replicate's float profiles are mapped as in Sukianto, Kuusela et al. (2026): the OHC of each layer
(15--700 m and 700--2000 m) minus the replicate's own local least-squares mean field is modelled, in each window, as a
zero-mean Gaussian process with the anisotropic exponential space-time covariance
$$
k\big((x,y,t),(x',y',t')\big) = \phi\,\exp\!\Big\{-\Big[\big(\tfrac{x-x'}{\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}}\big)^2
+ \big(\tfrac{y-y'}{\theta_{\mathrm{lat}}}\big)^2 + \big(\tfrac{t-t'}{\theta_t}\big)^2\Big]^{1/2}\Big\}
+ \sigma^2\,\mathbb{1}\{(x,y,t)=(x',y',t')\},
$$
with $x, y$ in degrees and $t$ in days. A window is a cell of the $2^\circ$ parameter grid and a calendar season
(DJF, MAM, JJA, SON, December counted with the following year): the profiles within $\pm 10^\circ$ of the cell centre
in the season's three calendar months, in each year 2015--2025. The years are independent blocks with common
parameters, so the log-likelihood is the sum over years of exact Gaussian log-likelihoods (years with at most 50
profiles in the window are dropped, and a window needs two years). Parameters are exact maximum-likelihood estimates,
by L-BFGS-B on the log-parameters from a single start; a second start reached the same optimum in all of 40 test
windows ($|\Delta\ell| < 0.01$).

The nugget estimate collapses to its lower bound in nearly every window (median $\sigma^2/\phi$ of
$1.3\times10^{-8}$ and $0.6\times10^{-8}$ in the two layers), as it should: simulated profiles are noise-free point
values of the GLORYS field, so there is no measurement error, and the nugget is not shown.

A replicate's plug-in for a cell is the median over its four seasonal fits. The **pooled plug-in** is the median over
all window fits of the cell across the ten replicates, between 24 and 40 fits (median 40); it is the plug-in used to
krige. Because it is fitted on replicates 0--9 only, kriging replicates 10--199 with it keeps the covariance parameters
external to the evaluated replicates. A fit has run away when a range parameter leaves the bounds of a physically
plausible window fit ($\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}, \theta_{\mathrm{lat}} \le 40^\circ$, $\theta_t \le 400$ days); such
cells, and cells with no fit, are left blank. No pooled cell is blank. Ranges are fitted in degrees (as in Sukianto,
Kuusela et al.) and mapped in km, $\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}\cdot\frac{\pi R}{180}\cos(\mathrm{lat})$ and
$\theta_{\mathrm{lat}}\cdot\frac{\pi R}{180}$ with $R = 6371$ km at the cell-centre latitude, so that a correlation
isotropic in distance shows equal zonal and meridional ranges.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Domain median of the pooled plug-ins (ranges in km and days), the range over replicates of the domain medians of their own plug-ins, the median over cells of the coefficient of variation of the ten replicates' plug-ins, and the number of blank replicate-cells (of 10 x 733)."

t = ns.cov_summary(REPS)
t["layer"] = t.layer.map(LAYER_LAB)
t["parameter"] = t.parameter.map(PAR_LAB)
display(Markdown(t.round(3).to_markdown(index=False)))
```

## Exact likelihood versus the Vecchia approximation

The earlier fits of replicates 0--4 used the Vecchia approximation (GpGp, `exponential_scaledim`, 30 neighbours) on
$\pm 45$-day windows centred on the 15th of January, April, July and October. Against the exact fits of the same five
replicates, the exact temporal range is 0.81 and 0.72 times the approximate one in the two layers and the exact
spatial ranges 1.09--1.15 times (cell medians). The windows also changed between the two (calendar seasons now), so
this ratio combines both effects; on 30 identical windows the approximation alone gave exact/approximate ratios of
0.83 for $\theta_t$ and about 1.05 for the spatial ranges.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-gpgp
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Domain medians of the pooled plug-ins of replicates 0-4 from the exact and Vecchia (GpGp) fits (ranges in km and days), and the median over cells of their ratio exact/GpGp."

t = ns.cov_vs_gpgp(REPS[:5])
t["layer"] = t.layer.map(LAYER_LAB)
t["parameter"] = t.parameter.map(PAR_LAB)
display(Markdown(t.round(3).to_markdown(index=False)))
```

## Comparison with Sukianto, Kuusela et al.

Our pooled plug-ins beside the published real-Argo estimates of Sukianto, Kuusela et al. (2026; Zenodo record
18273718, `MLE.zip`): the same exponential space-time model, fitted to Argo residuals about their harmonic-plus-trend
mean field for 2004--2022 on a $1^\circ$ grid, each a median over twelve monthly fits. Their values are the median of
the four $1^\circ$ cells in each of our $2^\circ$ cells, ranges are converted to km as above, and their variance
$\phi$ (unscaled, $(^\circ\mathrm{C}\,\mathrm{dbar})^2$) is multiplied by $(\rho_0 c_p)^2$ with their
$\rho_0 = 1030$ kg m$^{-3}$, $c_p = 3989.244$ J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, taking 1 dbar as 1 m. Their layers are 15--975 and
975--1850 dbar against our 15--700 and 700--2000 m, so the ranges are comparable but $\phi$ is not: it differs by
construction in level, and only its spatial pattern should be compared. Cells outside their data mask are blank.

```{python}
#| label: fig-kuusela
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

_layer_par_tabs(lambda l, p: ns.plot_cov_kuusela(REPS, l, p))
```
